_versionNote: Frozen at 0.0.1-alpha.0 until the first release. Do not bump it for ordinary changes — nothing is published, so there is no version anyone could be upgrading from. It must stay valid semver: npm's registry rejects anything else, and drift detection depends on ordered comparison.
_note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every pinned tool version. Nothing else in this repo hardcodes a version, and nothing resolves 'latest' at install time. To upgrade, see UPGRADING.md.
_policyNote: `policy` decides how strictly a version is held. "exact" for anything whose divergence corrupts the SHARED repo: rtk is a binary CoMind executes, gsd-core writes committed files, caveman installs hooks into ~/.claude. "floor" (>=) for machine-local tools whose output is derived — nobody's repo changes because a teammate has a newer graphify, and an exact pin there is a maintenance treadmill that buys nothing. Absent means exact.

distribution._note: How CoMind installs itself. The plugin path is primary because it gives uninstall, update, enable/disable, and a version registry for free; the file-copy fallback exists only for machines without the `claude` CLI. `marketplace add` accepts a URL, a path, or a GitHub repo: `--local` installs from this checkout (PKG_ROOT) and COMIND_MARKETPLACE overrides the source for a fork.

caveman._note: The COMMIT is the pin, not the tag. v1.9.1 = 0d95a81. Git tags are movable and the release reports "immutable": false, so a tag pin is a weaker promise than it looks. bin/install.js at this ref self-pins (PINNED_REF) and SHA-256-verifies every hook it downloads against the integrity manifest published at that ref, refusing to install on mismatch.
caveman._whyNotThePlugin: `claude plugin install` accepts no version, so the plugin path cannot pin. It stays as the fallback for machines without npx. The previous fallback was WORSE than unpinned: it fetched install.sh from the v1.9.1 tag, but that script execs a github package spec carrying NO #ref, which npm resolves to the default branch — so the "pinned" fallback installed main.

typescript._note: binName is required, not optional. Without it the installed-version probe cannot run, and the LSP layer treats the package as permanently missing — which made `npm install -g` re-run on every single setup.

lsp._note: Anthropic's first-party LSP plugins, from the auto-registered official marketplace. These replaced mcp-language-server, which was source-only (no release binaries at v0.1.0 or v0.1.1), required a Go toolchain, and could not report its own version. A plugin wraps a server binary but never ships one, so `server.bin` is what doctor probes and `server.manual` is the one line a developer runs when it is absent.
lsp._pinNote: Claude Code plugin installs cannot pin a version, so no version is recorded here. What actually determines diagnostics is the SERVER, and for the two npm-installable ones that stays pinned in `tools` above.
